Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE SECRETARY DILG OPINION NO. 44 s. 2mo 14 April 2010 ASEC. CIARITO L. MALLILLIN Finance and Comptrollership This Department Dear Sir: This has reference to your Memorandum dated 17 March 2009 requesting this level's comments/opinion on this issue, thus: "Are we to honor yet the vouchers signed by Undersecretary Melchor P. Rosales considering this COMELEC Resolution and the Supreme Court decision that party-list representatives/ nominees are considered resigned effective March g, 201 OP Further, from what date/s are we to reckon as basis of our "honoring/ recognizing" the vouchers signed by Undersecretary Rosales:' Is it "upon acceptance of his nomination by his Party-list'? "Or on March 26, 2010, the deadline set by COMELEC for all groups accredited to participate in the party-list elections to submit to the Commission's Law Department, their respective lists of not less than five nominees each from which the representatives shall be chosen in case it obtains the required number of votes. " It may be recalled that Usec. Melchor P. Rosales, Undersecretary for Peace and Order and Transnational Crime, this Department, is a nominee of APOI or Akbay Pinoy OFW Inc., a party-list for Overseas Filipino Workers. In reply to your queries, may we quote the pertinent portion of COMELEC Resolution No. 8697, entitled: "In the Matter of Providing the Rule on the Effects of Acceptance of Nomination by Party-List Nominees," promulgated on 11 November 2009, thus: "NOW, THEREFORE, the Commission RESOLVED as it hereby RESOLVES that: (1) (2) Party-list nominees who are holding public appointive office shall be considered ipso facto resigned upon their acceptance of their nomination. Nominees who are holding elective office may continue to hold office even after the acceptance of their nomination; The one year prohibition from being hired or rehired in a public office after their party-list organization fall to secure the needed votes to qualify them for a seat in the House of Representatives shall not apply to said nominees." (Emphasis Supplied)

-2- Based from the foregoing, a party-list nominee who is holding a public appointive office shall be considered ipso facto resigned upon his acceptance of his nomination. Thus, being an appointive official, upon acceptance of Usec. Rosales of his nomination as party-list representative of APOI, at that point in time, he is ipso facto resigned to his position as Undersecretary for Peace and Order and Transnational Crime. The term "ipso facto resigned" means that there is no need for him to perform an operative act, for example, that of filing or tendering his letter of resignation in the said position. The fact of accepting his nomination as party-list representative automatically makes him resigned. Upon his resignation to his position as Undersecretary for Peace and Order and Transnational Crime, Usec. Rosales shall accordingly cease and desist from performing the duties and functions appurtenant to said position, including that of signing vouchers. We hope we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. JESUS . DOQUE V Director III, Legal ServiCe us: 0/17
